correctness.rationale: Checked actual verifier path and its ten fraction-free Sylvester discriminants, Rabin finite-field irreducibility tests, cycle certificates for degrees four and six, discriminant primes valuation one, cubic factorization, and reciprocal symmetry. Transitive prime-degree groups are primitive; composite-degree rows have a (d-1,1) cycle and are primitive; tame simple discriminant ramification yields a transposition, so the group is S_d. For the exceptional pair, distinct quadratic subfields of the two S3 splitting fields imply linear disjointness. The n>=9 range is exactly the verified Garmi v1 theorem and is not inferred from finite checks.

value.rationale: Determining the sharp universal cutoff for an explicit infinite bounded-height polynomial family is a natural mathematical boundary problem: it settles all coprime indices at the first degree excluded by a fresh theorem, and the previously known n=7 exceptional factorization proves the cutoff optimal. This precise infinite-family threshold matters independently of code or the novelty of the arithmetic certificates; it is not claimed to be a new infinite-range theorem.
